 Main Card Results | Polymarket UFC 334: Gane vs Hokit
 Live Results, Highlights, Post-Fight Interviews With The Main Card Winners And More From Polymarket UFC 334: Gane vs Hokit, Live From Madison Square Garden On November 14, 2026 
 By E. Spencer Kyte, On X: @SpencerKyte
 • Nov. 15, 2026
 Following an entertaining preliminary card slate to start the night, Saturday’s Polymarket UFC 334 main card at Madison Square Garden was thoroughly entertaining, but also really weird, culminating in a chaotic main event clash for the undisputed UFC heavyweight title.
 Luis Gurule kicked things off by out-wrestling Bilal Hasan followed by Uros Medic and Kevin Holland fighting to a surprising draw and Caio Borralho earning a smart, tactical win over Yousri Belgaroui. In the co-main event, Kayla Harrison retained her women’s bantamweight title, turning back the challenge of the returning “Lioness” Amanda Nunes, and in the main event, Ciryl Gane dug deep to weather the storm created by Josh Hokit early in order to successfully defend his title.

 If you missed any of the action, check out our recaps below.
 Polymarket UFC 334 Results 
 More Coverage: Prelim Results | Official Scorecards 
 Ciryl Gane defeated Josh Hokit by unanimous decision (48-47, 48-47, 48-47) 
 Ciryl Gane rallied to defend the undisputed UFC heavyweight title with a hard-fought win over Josh Hokit .
 Hokit came out pushing a break-neck pace, staying in Gane’s face despite the big shots coming his way early, banking on the fact that he would tire the French technician out. While Gane landed well and at a higher clip than the challenger, Hokit’s assumption was correct and by the end of the first, the fight had turned into the kind of relentless chaos that favored the American challenger. Hokit continued to be the aggressor, finally getting to the point where he was landing the better blows in the third, only for Gane to have a much better round in the fourth, landing good knees to the body as Hokit’s output dipped.
 View on Threads 
 In the fifth, Gane continued to land the more impactful and significant blows, as Hokit’s energy meter emptied out and the champion started to really take over. To his credit, Hokit never stopped trying to connect and take the fight to Gane, landing a couple good shots late, but Gane wore them well and continued to press.
 After 25 rugged minutes, the judges were tasked with determining the victor, and when the scores were collected and totaled, it was Gane that emerged victorious, retaining the undisputed UFC heavyweight title. This was a gruelling, record-setting fight in terms of the number of strikes landed and thrown, and a fight where both men are able to take major positives away from their respective performances as we head towards what should be another fun year in the heavyweight ranks.
 Kayla Harrison defeated Amanda Nunes by submission (rear-naked choke) at 1:29 of Round 4 
 Kayla Harrison retained the UFC women’s bantamweight title, submitting Amanda Nunes in the fourth round of a gutsy battle by the champion.

 Kayla Harrison Submits Amanda Nunes To Defend Title | Polymarket UFC 334
 / 
 Live 
 Nunes came out striking from distance and having success initially, but I each of the first three rounds, she made the odd decision to tie up with Harrison as if she was looking to show she could beat the two-time Olympic gold medalist at her own game. Each time she did it, Harrison twisted her to the canvas and landed in a dominant position, finishing all three frames in top position, slicing her open in the third to head into the championship rounds clearly ahead on the scorecards. In the fourth, Harrison caught a kick and spilled Nunes to the canvas, chasing her down and taking the back, flattening her out and collecting the submission before the two had even really hit the ground.
 This was a gritty win for Harrison, who moved to 4-0 inside the Octagon and 20-1 overall with the victory, adding to her legacy as one of the greatest combat sport athletes ever. People are understandably going to question Nunes’ approach as it played against conventional wisdom, but all credit goes to Harrison for taking full advantage and chasing down the finish.
 Caio Borralho defeated Yousri Belgaroui by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27) 
 Caio Borralho brought Yousri Belgaroui's initial run of success to a halt on Saturday, leaning on his grappling and experience to secure a unanimous decision win in the final non-title clash of the night.

 Caio Borralho Post-Fight Interview | Polymarket UFC 334
 / 
 Live 
 The Fighting Nerd was tactical and strategic the whole way through, keeping Belgaroui off balance by landing occasional shots and changing levels at opportunistic times, working hard to control the lanky Dutch fighter on the canvas. Outside of a face crank in the first, Borralho wasn’t able to do too much when he did get the kickboxer to the canvas, the simple fact that he kept making Belgaroui work and defend was effective.
 It was a clean sweep of the scorecards for “The Natural,” who posted a career-best five takedowns on the way to collecting his second win of the year. While this win keeps Borralho stationed in the Top 5 of the middleweight division, it’ll be interesting to see what comes next after a low-output, grappling-heavy win.
 Uros Medic and Kevin Holland fought to a majority draw (29-27, 28-28, 28-28) 
 Uros Medi c and Kevin Holland fought to a surprising majority draw on Saturday, with many questioning the way the second round was scored.
 Kevin Holland and Uros Medic battle in their welterweight fight during the UFC 334 event at Madison Square Garden on November 14, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Zuffa LLC)
 Holland had his best success in the first, where he moved well and matched Medic’s striking output before getting deep on a D’arce choke attempt that stands as the highlight of the contest. A pair of accidental low blows brought about a five-minute pause in the action in the second and cost Medic a point, with the Serbian doing his best to try and chase down a finish in the third.
 The scorecards were initially announced wrong, but the result was correct, with even the broadcasters caught off guard. In the end, two officials scored the second 9-9 following the deduction, resulting in the twin 28-28 cards. A weird fight got a weird outcome, with neither man being saddled with a loss to end their 2026 campaigns.
 Luis Gurule defeated Bilal Hasan by split decision (28-29, 29-28, 29-28) 
 Luis Gurule continued the trend of more seasoned competitors defeating their more hyped, inexperienced foes on Saturday night, grinding out a good win over Season 10 Contender Series grad Bilal Hasan , handing him the first loss of his career.

 Luis Gurule Post-Fight Interview | Polymarket UFC 334
 /

 Hasan won the first handily, dominating the action on the feet, despite getting dropped at one point by Gurule. But over the second and third, “Grim” did well to close the distance and ground the striker, mauling him on the canvas and staying active enough to maintain the position while shutting down Hasan’s offense.
 Two of the three judges scored the fight in favor of Gurule, who entered as a considerable underdog and picked up his second win in four starts this year. This will be a good learning experience for Hasan, who is only 25 and still developing, especially on the ground, but Saturday night belonged to the Colorado-based veteran.
